question: How many vacation days can employees carry forward?
expected_answer: Employees may carry forward up to five unused vacation days into the next calendar year.

question: What happens to unused vacation days above the carryover limit?
expected_answer: Unused vacation days above the five-day carryover limit normally expire at the end of the calendar year.

question: Can an employee get an exception to the vacation carryover limit?
expected_answer: Yes. An exception may be granted when business circumstances prevented the employee from taking approved leave, subject to manager and HR approval.

question: Who can approve an exception to the annual leave policy?
expected_answer: Exceptions are subject to both manager and HR approval.

question: What are the requirements for working remotely?
expected_answer: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval. Some roles may require additional on-site attendance, and remote work arrangements may be reviewed or modified.

question: How many days per week can an employee work remotely?
expected_answer: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval.

question: What happens if business requirements prevent an employee from using accrued leave?
expected_answer: The manager may request an exception to the standard five-day carryover limit, and approved exceptions must be documented and submitted to HR.

question: Who may request an exception to the standard five-day vacation carryover limit?
expected_answer: The manager may request an exception when documented business requirements prevented the employee from using accrued leave.

question: What is the role of a manager in ensuring annual leave is used?
expected_answer: Managers should make reasonable efforts to ensure employees can use their annual leave during the applicable leave year.

question: Can an employee carry forward ten vacation days into the next calendar year?
expected_answer: No. The standard carryover limit is five unused vacation days; days above that limit normally expire at the end of the calendar year.
